text:
jamie_liao: kicking off HeliosBank POC commit thread. sales wants a conservative committed GPU recommendation, autoscale snippet for SOW, and a short security line about preheat/KV. profile below.

nina_cho: traffic profile: steady 60 rps (3600 req/min). short bursts up to 700 rps for 60-180s, ~3x/day. avg tokens/request 420, heavy tail up to 1400. mix: 70% short-turn chat, 30% long generations.

omar_singh: perf note: target model M-XL-2 quantized @ safe 11k tokens/s per A100-equivalent. use 10k t/s for planning overhead. baseline tokens/s = 60*420 = 25_200 -> 25_200/10_000 = 2.52 -> ~3 GPUs baseline.

trent_wells: bursts math: peak 700*420 = 294_000 t/s -> 29.4 GPUs peak. obviously we need autoscale + burst credits; reserved commit should cover steady+SLA buffer. my recommendation: reserved=9 (3x steady) pinned across AZs + burst credit pool and rapid autoscale to handle peaks.

jamie_liao: sales asks for a 3-line cost summary: reserve 3 vs reserve 9 vs reserve1+burst. can you draft concise lines for the deck?

trent_wells: sure: 
- reserve 3 GPUs: lower monthly commit, expected variable GPU-hours + token spend ~+45% during spikes, p95 latency variable (likely 400-700ms spikes).
- reserve 9 GPUs: higher commit fee, ~20% lower variable costs vs reserve3, predictable p95 (~<250ms typical) and AZ outage tolerance for single-AZ events.
- reserve 1 + burst: lowest commit fee, highest variable spend (~+60%+), best for cost-sensitivity but not SLA-friendly.

omar_singh: autoscale snippet for SOW (pasteable):
```
autoscale_policy:
  reserved_gpus: 9
  min_gpus: 1
  burst_credit_pool: 3000            # tokenized units to cover short spikes
  scale_up_condition: p95_latency_ms > 300 OR queue_depth > 80
  scale_down_condition: p95_latency_ms < 220 for 7m
  preheat_kv_warm: true
  kv_seed_strategy: top_percentile=25, data_source=synthetic
  az_affinity: spread_across=2
```

nina_cho: security Q: customer wants explicit wording confirming preheat doesn't touch customer PII. can we provide a one-line?

omar_singh: one-liner: "KV preheat and seed jobs use anonymized synthetic prefixes and, for Dedicated/Private deployments, run within the customer's network boundary; Redwood-managed preheat jobs do not receive or store customer PII."

trent_wells: ops note: with reserved=9 pinned across 2 AZs we can sustain a single-AZ capacity reduction for short windows; for sustained AZ loss we recommend cross-region failover (procedural or automated depending on the contract). include in runbook.

jamie_liao: sales also asked whether we can run a preheat that seeds customer-specific prefixes without uploading data. answer?

omar_singh: we can provide a customer-executed preheat job: run the KV-seed container inside their VPC (customer supplies seed list locally) so nothing leaves their network. add as an option in SOW.

opsbot: infra-bot: preheat template hel-preheat-4943216789 created; will schedule when commit accepted. :white_check_mark:

jamie_liao: action items: (1) trent post a short 3-line cost table to the sales deck (2) omar attach safe autoscale snippet to SOW (3) nina include the security one-liner + optional customer-executed preheat wording. i'll loop with sales in 18h. :thumbsup:
